chosen.title: The Satellite Factory: Inside the Robotic Assembly Line That Builds a Spacecraft in 30 Hours
chosen.rationale: China just switched on its first fully automated satellite production line, collapsing assembly time from seven days to 30 hours to feed megaconstellations — a car-factory model for spacecraft that sits dead-center in Kenji's aerospace + robotics + advanced-manufacturing beat and his love of *where and how things actually get built*. It's brand new (Aug 27, 2026) and distinct from the covered orbital-data-center and aerospace-metal-forming pieces because the story is throughput and industrialization of orbit, not a single part or a power problem.

rejected_candidates.title: The Mind in Orbit: How Autonomous AI Learned to Fly Satellites Without Us
rejected_candidates.rationale: Shield AI just flew its Hivemind autonomy stack on the NOVI satellite in orbit (Aug 24, 2026), with a physics simulator vetting every command before execution — the moment edge-AI decision-making moved off Earth and onto the spacecraft itself. It hits Kenji's exact trifecta (AI + aerospace + autonomous systems), gives him a real mechanism to unpack, and comes with a built-in honest reckoning: the company is a defense contractor, so autonomous judgment in orbit carries genuine stakes.
